quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When riding in a group, riders should be:
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding. It keeps riders close together while giving each rider enough space. Use single-file formation when turning, entering a highway, or exiting a highway.

questions.question: When braking on a motorcycle:

options.text: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when slowing down or stopping. If you only use the rear brake, you won't develop the skill to use the front brake when you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT significantly affect your blood alcohol content (BAC)?
questions.explanation: BAC is affected by how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. Age does not play a major role.

questions.question: To properly control a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Use your arms to hold up your body.
Keep your knees against the fuel tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the fuel tank.
questions.explanation: Sit with your arms slightly bent. Use your arms to steer, not to support your weight. Keep your knees against the fuel tank to help balance during turns.

questions.question: Locking your brakes can:
questions.explanation: Locked brakes cause control problems. If your front brake locks, release it and re-apply it quickly. If your rear brake locks on good pavement, keep it locked until you stop.

questions.question: When a tailgater is following you, you should:
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. Speeding up won't help—they'll just tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: How do convex mirrors differ from regular mirrors?
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors provide a wider view of the road than flat mirrors. However, they can make vehicles behind you look farther away than they really are.

questions.question: A motorcycle's brake light is _________ a car's brake light.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are usually less noticeable than car brake lights, especially when the taillight is on. Other drivers may not notice your brake light, so stay alert.

questions.question: When riding, wear boots or shoes that:
questions.explanation: Riding shoes should be high and sturdy to cover and support your ankles. Heels should be low so they don't catch on surfaces. Shoelaces should be tucked in to prevent them from getting caught.

questions.question: When making a U-turn:

options.text: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Don't use the front brake because it could tip the bike over.
Use the front brake to make the motorcycle more stable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't use the front brake because it could tip the bike over.
questions.explanation: Don't use the front brake during a U-turn because it could cause the bike to tip. Use only the rear brake to control your speed during the U-turn.

questions.question: What is the best way to make sure others can see your motorcycle?

options.text: Use your headlight only at night or when visibility is poor.
Add an orange tint to your headlight.

questions.explanation: The best way to help others see your motorcycle is to ride with your headlight on all the time.

questions.question: If you are towing a trailer on your motorcycle, your following distance should:
questions.explanation: When towing a trailer, you should increase your following distance. The extra weight means your motorcycle needs more time to stop.

questions.question: Should you wear gloves when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Yes. Your hands may get cold while riding.
Yes. They give you a better grip and protect your hands.
No. Gloves can interfere with the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes. They give you a better grip and protect your hands.
questions.explanation: Gloves give you a better grip and help protect your hands. Use full-fingered gloves made of durable material.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell you about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: What can a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect you from?
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your face in a crash. It also protects you from stones thrown by other vehicles, wind, dust, dirt, rain, and insects.

questions.question: When riding in the rain, where should you ride?

options.text: In the center of your lane.
On the right side of your lane.
In the tire tracks left by other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the tire tracks left by other cars.
questions.explanation: Roads are very slippery when rain first starts. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars to get better traction.

questions.question: If another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the center portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. It is the safest position. Riding on the side near the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding on the far side may make the driver return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell you about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that the road ahead is slippery when wet.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell you about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that the right lane ends ahead.

questions.question: Where is the greatest risk of conflict between your motorcycle and other vehicles?
questions.explanation: The greatest risk of conflict between a motorcycle and other vehicles is at intersections.

questions.question: When parked on the road, how should a motorcycle be positioned?

options.text: At an angle of 45 to 90 degrees to the curb.
Without any wheel or fender touching the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: At an angle of 45 to 90 degrees to the curb.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle should be parked at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees to the curb. At least one wheel or fender should touch the curb.

questions.question: What is the best way to help others see your motorcycle during normal riding?

options.text: Keep your high beam headlight on.
Paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your high beam headlight on.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times, day and night, when it is legal and safe. Use your high beam to make your motorcycle more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: When stopping your motorcycle with a passenger, what should you do?

options.text: Ride faster than you normally would.
Begin slowing down earlier than you normally would.
Merge into smaller traffic gaps than you normally would.

questions.correctAnswerText: Begin slowing down earlier than you normally would.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. This extra weight makes the motorcycle slower to speed up, slow down, and turn. Start slowing down earlier when stopping. Also look for larger traffic gaps when crossing, entering, or merging into traffic.

questions.question: What color and lettering do service signs have?
questions.explanation: Service signs are blue with white letters. They show where you can find rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: What should you do when lights are flashing at a railroad crossing sign?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Turn around and find a different route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: When lights flash at a railroad crossing, stop completely. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before you go. Never try to drive around a train.
